newsitem.title: FRANCE: France protests Bosnian Serb's presence at embassy.
newsitem.headline: France protests Bosnian Serb's presence at embassy.

text.p: Paris protested to Bosnian Serb authorities on Saturday against the uninvited presence at France's embassy in Sarajevo of a Bosnian Serb officer held responsible for the torture of French U.N. peacekeepers.

A foreign ministry spokesman said an energetic protest was being made about Bosnian Serb commander General Pero Colic, invited to an embassy reception this month, arriving with Colonel Milenko Indic who was involved in the taking hostage of hundreds of U.N. peacekeepers in Bosnia in May 1995.
The foreign ministry statement came after the influential daily Le Monde wrote in a front-page article that French officers in Sarajevo were furious when they saw Indic arrive at the embassy.

The daily said the officers held Indic responsible for such tortures of captive French soldiers during the 1995 crisis as beatings, cigarette burns, simulated executions and pushing a junior officer's face into the stomach of a corpse.

Le Monde said the army had so far kept secret from the public testimony from the soldiers but officers had sworn they would take revenge against Indic, now a main Bosnian-Serb liaison officer with international bodies.

"We want an investigation into this matter and reserve the right to take the necessary measures before the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia about the events mentioned in newspaper articles," the foreign ministry spokesman said.
"If the Quai d'Orsay (the French foreign ministry) doesn't know exactly who the people are who it meets, French officers have not forgotten," Le Monde wrote.
The foreign ministry's apparently embarrassed statement said the reception was attended by officers from all former warring sides and "showed the new realities in Sarajevo."
The May 1995 crisis, in which soldiers from many countries were taken hostage, led to fighting between U.N. forces and the Bosnian Serbs.
This led ultimately to the start of a U.S.-led aerial bombing capaign which forced the Bosnian Serbs to sue for a truce which led to the current halt in hostilities.
